- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.6) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤0.2) or volatile (alternating ±0.4+), model often underestimates; add 1–3% to forecast for next 3–5 days.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 1–2 days); cap forecast at +3% above recent peak for next 3 days.
- If 3–5 consecutive days show mean reversion (price moving back toward 60–65 range), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with recent 5-day average.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates in high-sentiment periods; apply +2–5% bias if sentiment >0.6 over last 7 days.
- If sentiment history shows “reversal” (e.g., +0.8 → -0.4 → +0.6), model often misreads momentum; reduce forecast 1–2% for next 3 days.
